title: Omaha bandleaders required married men; Holland Harold
summary: Leaders in Omaha refused unmarried musicians, so he ended up working with Holland Harold, who helped his musical education.

bands.name: Red Perkins and His Eight Fabulous Musicians

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What time was your first marriage, when you finally met your wife - your first wife?

Milt, I wasn't going to marry nobody. It was impossible. But I ran into a situation in Omaha, Nebraska. Omaha, Nebraska gave me an education, for nearly Four years, from '30 up until the time I went to Kansas City. Everywhere I went and tried to get into a band, the band-leader would say, "Son, are you married?" You talk about Branch Rickey. I'd say, "No, I'm not married. I'm not marrying nobody." He'd say, "You have to be married to be in this band." So finally -
There was one of the greatest men that ever lived, was Holland Harold. He had the group that when he became ill and his son was playing with Hunter's Serenaders.
But I hadn't joined the Hunter's Serenaders because Al was there but I played with his father's band.
Was Mr. Holland Harold a drummer?

Holland Harold, Tubby, that's right, and he taught me. He was the second greatest man. He was the man who helped me with my musical education and - I wasn't going to marry nobody. Then there was the Night Owls. There was Red Perkins and his 8 fabulous musicians which was a unit. Everywhere I turned there were people telling me I had to get married. I wasn't going to marry nobody. So finally after making 6 feeble attempts in 2 months, I married! I married June 23rd, 1933. I begged the girl; I said, now wait a minute. I told you I'd marry a woman with a whole lot of money, or marry you. I said, "Will you do me a favor?" "What?" "Just marry me."
